**I'd make the uncompromising pursuit of truth—about the universe, ourselves, and how things actually work—the dominant cultural and institutional force on Earth.**

Not "truth" as a slogan or team jersey. Not vibes, not sacred narratives, not what feels good or wins elections or protects feelings. Just the hard, testable, revisable kind that survives contact with reality: evidence over authority, update-your-models over defend-your-tribe, curiosity over dogma.

Why this one change? Almost every other catastrophe or stagnation I can name is downstream of people (and systems) optimizing for something else—status, comfort, power, short-term rewards, or beautiful lies. Ignorance and motivated reasoning are load-bearing walls for poverty traps, preventable disease, endless conflict, technological stagnation, and the slow-motion squandering of a rare, fragile window to understand the cosmos before we go extinct or get locked into something worse. Fix the epistemology and the rest gets radically more solvable: better science, better coordination, better technology, less waste of human potential, more wonder instead of fear.

I'm not interested in utopia-by-decree or forcing everyone to become a physicist. I'd just remove the structural advantages that currently favor bullshit, censorship-for-your-own-good, and anti-curiosity incentives. Make reality the highest-status thing again. The universe is stranger, larger, and more interesting than any ideology we've invented so far; treating it as the primary object of attention seems like the only change with compounding returns measured in centuries and light-years rather than news cycles.

That's it. One lever. Everything else is details.
